project.title: Investment Committee Simulation
project.subtitle: Three approval gates. Five committee members. One integrated recommendation.
project.premise: Your five-person investment committee advises three client mandates and manages $500,000 in hypothetical assets. The committee must establish a market view, build and challenge each portfolio, and defend one evidence-linked recommendation.
project.scopeNote: Canvas remains the authority for due dates, submission links, and course-grade weights.

studentRoadmap.title: Your Project Roadmap
studentRoadmap.subtitle: Follow the decision path. Build the analysis. Defend your recommendation.

visual.alt: Investment Committee Simulation roadmap showing Phase 1 mandate approval, Phase 2 focused 8–10 holding selection, portfolio integration, stress testing and hedge or no-hedge conclusion, Phase 3 presentation and compact defense, and five distinct committee roles.

studentRoadmap.boundary: BUS331 provides structured Excel workbooks and client data. Your committee completes the analysis, reaches its own conclusions, and creates its own final PowerPoint presentation.
beforeYouBegin: Confirm the five committee roles and your three assigned clients.
Create a shared team workspace and agree on a file-naming system.
Read the current phase checklist together before beginning work.
Schedule a short committee meeting before each approval gate.

phase-1: Set roles, client assignments, and the team workspace.
Complete the detailed macro analysis in the provided workbook: review historical evidence, form a human-first interpretation, and document sources.
Compare the committee view with FactSet and/or FRED evidence, then create bull, base, and bear scenarios with probabilities totaling 100%.
Analyze each client's goals, constraints, risk, and unresolved information gaps.
Translate the macro outlook into a client-specific mandate, including return target, risk limit, and drawdown tripwire.
Hold Gate 1: challenge the evidence, vote, and record required revisions before any portfolio construction begins.
phase-2: Reopen the approved client mandate before researching investments.
Use the structured workbooks to develop capital-market expectations and draft allocations.
Translate each approved allocation and client mandate into a candidate set, then compare serious alternatives against client guardrails.

Select 8–10 final holdings per portfolio, never more than 10, using funds and ETFs as the primary vehicles; limit individual securities to two or three total and add at most one targeted derivative hedge only when justified.

Build the proposed portfolios, identify the purpose and concise scorecard for every final holding, resolve overlap and concentration, and submit the locked baseline snapshot before the Scenario Reveal.
After the instructor releases the client-specific Scenario Reveal, apply its exact inputs, identify the client consequence, correct the required breach, and re-test.
Hold Gate 2: approve, revise, or reject each client portfolio and record the decision.
phase-3: Convert approved analysis into a clear committee recommendation for each client.
Create the decision memo and technical evidence package.
Design and build the committee's own visual PowerPoint presentation.
Rehearse cross-functional questions and the strongest trade-offs.
Hold Gate 3, submit the required package in Canvas, and defend the recommendation.

phase-1: The macro workbook documents historical analysis, consensus comparison, and weighted bull, base, and bear scenarios.
Each client has objectives, RRTTLLU constraints, a return target, risk limit, drawdown tripwire, and identified information gaps.
The committee can explain how its macro outlook changes each client mandate.
All five members have recorded the Gate 1 vote and any revision actions.
phase-2: Each client portfolio traces back to an approved mandate and has a stated purpose for every holding.

Each portfolio has 8–10 final holdings, never more than 10, with no requirement to fill every slot; funds and ETFs are the primary vehicles and individual securities are limited to two or three total.
Every final holding has a concise scorecard, rejected alternatives have a concise comparison, and the team has resolved unnecessary overlap or concentration.

Any derivative hedge is limited to one targeted residual risk and documents instrument, size, cost, liquidity, trade-offs, residual risk, and adjustment or removal condition; a supported no-hedge conclusion is equally complete.
The baseline snapshot was submitted before the Scenario Reveal; each revealed-scenario breach has a documented corrective trade, trade-off, and full re-test.
All five members have recorded the Gate 2 vote and any revision actions.
phase-3: The memo, evidence package, and presentation tell one consistent recommendation story.
A reviewer can trace each major claim to evidence.
Every member has rehearsed and can defend both owned work and the integrated decision.
The team has checked Canvas for the correct required files and deadline.

roles.title: Client and Macro Strategist
roles.mandate: Own client discovery, the 12-month market view, IPS objectives and constraints, and the handoff from client needs to investment criteria.

phaseResponsibilities.phase-1: Lead the client interview, document goals and RRTTLLU constraints, establish the macro context, and name unresolved information gaps.
phaseResponsibilities.phase-2: Test whether proposed allocations and securities fit the approved client mandate and the committee's market view.
phaseResponsibilities.phase-3: Defend client suitability, the macro assumptions, and the line from discovered need to recommendation.

roles.title: Fixed-Income Analyst
roles.mandate: Own the income, capital-preservation, maturity, duration, credit-quality, liquidity, and tax questions that shape the fixed-income sleeve.

phaseResponsibilities.phase-1: Translate cash-flow needs, time horizon, liquidity, taxes, and loss capacity into fixed-income questions and provisional guardrails.
phaseResponsibilities.phase-2: Analyze yields, duration, credit, liquidity, and structure; recommend fixed-income exposures that meet the approved guardrails.
phaseResponsibilities.phase-3: Defend the portfolio's income, capital-preservation, interest-rate, and credit-risk trade-offs.

roles.title: Equity Analyst
roles.mandate: Own equity-fund and ETF due diligence and the limited use of individual equities, including exposure, style, sector, holdings, costs, liquidity, overlap, idiosyncratic risk, and position-size evidence.

phaseResponsibilities.phase-1: Translate the client's growth needs, time horizon, values, tax position, liquidity, and concentration limits into equity-selection guardrails.
phaseResponsibilities.phase-2: Recommend equity funds and ETFs as the primary equity vehicles and analyze any limited individual equities, including rationale, idiosyncratic risk, and position size.
phaseResponsibilities.phase-3: Defend equity exposures, vehicle choices, limited individual-security decisions, rejected alternatives, and their client fit.

roles.title: Portfolio Manager
roles.mandate: Own portfolio integration: resolve overlap and concentration, set final selection and weights, record explicit trade-offs, maintain decision-log quality, and move the integrated recommendation to a vote.

phaseResponsibilities.phase-1: Reconcile risk capacity and willingness, set provisional portfolio guardrails, coordinate the committee challenge, and audit the Analyst Decision Log.
phaseResponsibilities.phase-2: Integrate analyst recommendations, resolve duplication and concentration, choose the final 8–10 holdings and weights, and record the trade-offs behind every integration decision.
phaseResponsibilities.phase-3: State and defend the integrated recommendation, portfolio construction decisions, final weights, rejected integrations, and implementation priorities.

roles.title: Risk and Derivatives Analyst
roles.mandate: Own portfolio-level risk diagnosis, stress testing, residual-risk evidence, mandate-breach escalation, and the hedge or no-hedge conclusion; do not manufacture a derivative position when no targeted hedge is justified.

phaseResponsibilities.phase-1: Define the downside questions, drawdown tripwire, stress priorities, and residual-risk evidence the final portfolio must address.
phaseResponsibilities.phase-2: Run portfolio-level stress tests, identify residual risk, and document either one targeted hedge or a fully supported no-hedge conclusion, including cost, liquidity, trade-offs, residual risk, and adjustment or removal conditions.
phaseResponsibilities.phase-3: Defend the stress evidence, residual risk, hedge or no-hedge decision, limits of the analysis, and conditions that would change the risk response.

committeeProtocol.description: Circulate the required evidence before the meeting. Every member reviews the full package.
The workstream lead states a clear recommendation and cites the evidence that supports it.

The Portfolio Manager coordinates the strongest counterargument; the analyst whose judgment is challenged must respond with evidence, and the Risk and Derivatives Analyst independently tests the residual risk.
The phase lead states the motion. The Portfolio Manager records approve, revise, or reject; all five members vote and any non-approval vote requires revision.
Capture evidence reviewed, dissent or reservations, owners, and actions before the next gate.

phase1Experience.title: Client Discovery and Decision Protocol
phase1Experience.subtitle: Interview the client. Challenge the first answer. Verify the evidence. Set the guardrails.
phase1Experience.purpose: Turn a fictional client profile into documented investment criteria before the team screens a bond, mutual fund, ETF, or portfolio allocation.

clientSets.inquiry: Investigate how near-term spending, concentrated wealth, and overlapping goals change the meaning of risk.
Investigate how illiquidity, taxes, a known cash need, and retirement urgency constrain an otherwise attractive return target.
Investigate how experience, values, variable income, and emergency reserves affect capacity, willingness, and product fit.
Investigate how loss aversion, currency exposure, relocation, taxes, and restricted holdings affect implementable choices.
Investigate how philanthropy, debt, uneven cash flow, starting capital, and multigenerational goals change portfolio priorities.

structuredRolePlay.clientRule: The student playing the client uses only the sealed client card. If the card does not establish an answer, say: ‘That is not established in my brief.’ Do not invent a fact or recommend an investment.
structuredRolePlay.analystRule: The other committee members ask their own open, neutral questions, take notes, and record evidence, assumptions, and information gaps.
structuredRolePlay.recordRule: After each interview, the committee records a concise summary—not a word-for-word transcript—in the Analyst Decision Log.

instructorDemo.name: Sally Hart
instructorDemo.caseLabel: Classroom demonstration · not an assigned client
instructorDemo.identity: Fictional client for practicing the interview process
instructorDemo.statedDirection: Practice asking neutral questions and identifying information gaps before teams begin their assigned cases.
instructorDemo.clientCue: Sally is candid, thoughtful, and occasionally unsure. She answers only what the practice card establishes and never recommends investments.
openingQuestions: What matters most to you about this money?
What future need should we plan around first?
What would make a loss difficult for you?

rolePlaySequence.action: Before teams begin, the instructor gives one volunteer the sealed Sally Hart client card. The class observes a short interview, pauses to identify established facts and information gaps, and records one sample client guardrail.

After macro analysis, each team receives three sealed client cards. For the first case, the Client and Macro Strategist begins as the client; the other four members act as analysts. Do not open a card assigned to another student.

Run a 12-minute interview for each client. Rotate the client role for the second and third cases so different members experience the client perspective. The Portfolio Manager keeps the decision-log record consistent across all three cases.
After each interview, all five members identify established facts, information gaps, and provisional guardrails. Challenge the first interpretation as a committee before moving to the next client.
Use the three interview summaries, the macro outlook, and the assigned case files to complete the IPS analysis and prepare for Gate 1.

decisionCycle.action: Read the assigned client profile and record one tentative, evidence-based interpretation: what the client needs, which constraints matter, and what remains unknown.
decisionCycle.logEvidence: The interpretation; supporting case evidence and assumptions; unanswered questions; and the portfolio or security decision it could affect

decisionCycle.action: Watch the instructor-led practice interview and notice how neutral questions reveal facts, expose information gaps, and lead to a provisional guardrail.
decisionCycle.logEvidence: One established fact, one information gap, and one possible guardrail from the classroom model

decisionCycle.action: Open your team page. The designated client uses the sealed card; the other members ask their own open, neutral questions and rotate the client role across the three cases.
decisionCycle.logEvidence: Question themes and response summary—not a word-for-word transcript

decisionCycle.action: As a committee, test the first interpretation, separate facts from assumptions, and verify material claims in the assigned files, team workbook, or approved source.
decisionCycle.logEvidence: Material challenge; source or file location; source date; and Confirmed / Qualified / Contradicted / Not verifiable

decisionCycle.action: State what changed, what remains uncertain, the final judgment, and the guardrail that later security selection or portfolio construction must honor.
decisionCycle.logEvidence: Final decision, concise rationale, downstream guardrail, and peer review

questionThemes: Tax, legal, values, and other unique constraints
Macro conditions that could change the plan
interviewRounds.handoff: Draft the client objective, the RRTTLLU facts, and a list of facts still missing.

questionThemes: Tolerance for price changes when rates move
interviewRounds.handoff: Draft the provisional maturity, duration, credit-quality, liquidity, and income guardrails.

questionThemes: Long-term growth need and equity-loss capacity
Sector, style, values, and benchmark restrictions
Fee, tax, trading, and liquidity sensitivity
Conditions for any limited individual-security exposure
interviewRounds.handoff: Draft the screen for equity funds and ETFs and any limited individual equity; do not name a winning product yet.

questionThemes: Ability and willingness to bear loss
interviewRounds.handoff: Reconcile conflicts, identify portfolio-level trade-offs, and specify which selection or weighting decisions require committee approval.

interviewRounds.round: Downside, residual risk, and hedge conditions
questionThemes: Client goal most exposed in a bear case
Residual risks the client can or cannot accept
Conditions under which a targeted hedge could be justified or removed
interviewRounds.handoff: Propose the drawdown tripwire, name the residual risks to stress, and identify which facts must be verified before any hedge or no-hedge conclusion.

committeeChallengeQuestions: What is the strongest reasonable interpretation that contradicts our initial judgment? Separate case facts from assumptions.
Which client answer may reflect willingness to take risk but not financial capacity—or the reverse? What evidence would resolve the conflict?
Which claim, number, or product characteristic cannot be accepted until a human checks an approved source?
How could this proposed guardrail fail to protect the client's most important goal in a bear case?
What later bond, mutual-fund/ETF, or allocation decision would change if this assumption is wrong?

approvedSources.label: Assigned fictional client files
approvedSources.use: Client facts, goals, constraints, and case-specific values

approvedSources.label: Team workbooks
approvedSources.use: Team calculations, scenarios, and model outputs
approvedSources.source: Use an exact sheet and cell or table location

approvedSources.label: FactSet
approvedSources.use: Course-authorized market, security, fund, and consensus data
approvedSources.source: Record the data item, entity, as-of date, and FactSet workspace

approvedSources.label: FRED, BLS, BEA, and U.S. Treasury
approvedSources.use: Macroeconomic series, releases, and Treasury rates

approvedSources.label: SEC EDGAR and issuer filings
approvedSources.use: Company disclosures, risks, financial statements, and filed fund documents

approvedSources.label: Official fund sponsor documents
approvedSources.use: Prospectus objective, benchmark, holdings, expenses, risks, distributions, and tax disclosures
approvedSources.source: Cite the official prospectus, summary prospectus, annual report, or fund page with an as-of date

cfaFoundations.application: Understand the client's objectives and constraints before asset allocation and security analysis.
Connect business-cycle and macroeconomic conditions to the client's decision context without treating forecasts as facts.
Use cash-flow features, yield measures, interest-rate risk, liquidity, and credit analysis to frame later bond decisions.
Compare mutual funds and ETFs as implementation vehicles and examine diversification, benchmark, cost, liquidity, and fit.
Separate risk capacity from willingness, document a reasonable basis, challenge uncertainty, and preserve client-first reasoning.

decisionLogFields: Case fact, assumption, or market claim
qualityGate: Each role records at least one human-first judgment for each assigned client before the structured role-play.
Every material committee challenge is summarized in the Analyst Decision Log; a role-play conversation is not a substitute for analysis.
Every factual claim or number used in the final reasoning has an approved source and as-of date.
Unknown client information remains labeled unknown; it is not filled with invented detail.
The final reasoning states what changed the judgment and why.
Each final judgment creates a testable guardrail for later fixed-income, equity, allocation, stress-test, or hedge/no-hedge decisions.
A second team member reviews the evidence trail before the Phase 1 gate.

phase2Experience.title: Security Selection, Portfolio Integration, and Risk Testing
phase2Experience.subtitle: Translate the mandate. Compare serious alternatives. Select a focused portfolio. Test the residual risk.
phase2Experience.handoffRule: No candidate security or portfolio weight may be approved unless the team identifies the Phase 1 client need, constraint, unresolved question, or downstream guardrail it addresses.
requiredInputs: Approved client objective and RRTTLLU constraints
Required and desired return, maximum volatility, and drawdown tripwire
Liquidity dates, cash-flow needs, tax considerations, values, and unique constraints
Committee base and bear macro scenarios with source dates
Phase 1 Analyst Decision Log, including unresolved information gaps and downstream guardrails

securityWorkflow.action: Turn each Phase 1 guardrail and the approved allocation into a measurable screen before researching products. Separate must-pass constraints from preferences.

Translate the approved allocation and client mandate into a focused candidate set. Funds and ETFs are the primary vehicles; individual securities are limited implementation choices, and individual bonds are not required.
Use a concise, consistent scorecard for each serious finalist. Compare and reject alternatives briefly; do not complete a full scorecard for every screened name.
Make a provisional choice first, then use AI to surface the strongest counterargument, missing risk, or contradictory interpretation.
Check every material AI-assisted claim in an approved source, then accept, modify, or reject the provisional choice and record why.
State the finalist's portfolio purpose, proposed weight, scorecard conclusion, key trade-off, client-fit condition, and the event that would trigger review or removal.

selectionContract.portfolioSize: Target 8–10 final holdings per client portfolio and never exceed 10. Eight is a valid complete portfolio; do not add a holding merely to fill a slot.
selectionContract.vehicleMix: Funds and ETFs are the primary implementation vehicles. Individual securities are permitted only when they add a distinct, mandate-aligned benefit and are limited to two or three total per portfolio. Individual bonds are not required.
inclusionBoundaries: Every holding has a distinct purpose in the portfolio and fits the approved client mandate.
The holding adds useful exposure or diversification without unnecessary duplication or concentration.
The position and its underlying exposure have liquidity appropriate to the client and the planned weight.
The holding's cost, trading expenses, risks, and implementation demands are proportionate to its benefit.
scorecardFields: Exposure and role in the portfolio
individualSecurityAdditions: Why an individual security is superior to a fund or ETF for this specific role
selectionContract.alternativeStandard: Compare the strongest realistic alternatives and record why they were rejected in one concise decision record. Full scorecards are required for final holdings, not every screened name.

instrumentStandards.instrument: Fixed-income fund, ETF, or limited direct exposure
instrumentStandards.decisionQuestion: Does the exposure fit the client's income, capital-preservation, duration, credit, liquidity, tax, and rate-risk guardrails?
requiredAnalysis: Fund or ETF objective, benchmark, holdings, cost, liquidity, and income characteristics; use direct-bond terms only if a direct bond is actually proposed
Yield or income measure and the return drivers under the base and bear macro cases
Duration or interest-rate sensitivity and the effect of a rate move
Credit quality, spread, downgrade/default, and concentration risk
Overlap, diversification contribution, client fit, proposed portfolio role, and monitoring trigger
Concise alternative rejected and the key trade-off

instrumentStandards.decisionQuestion: Does the vehicle deliver the intended equity exposure efficiently without hidden concentration, overlap, trading, liquidity, tax, or style problems?
requiredAnalysis: Objective, benchmark or index methodology, style, sector, region, and active or passive approach
Top holdings, concentration, sector/style overlap, and diversification contribution
Expense ratio, trading expenses, turnover, distributions, and tax considerations
Liquidity at both the vehicle and underlying-holdings level
Performance or tracking context using comparable periods and current as-of dates
Client fit, portfolio role, monitoring trigger, concise rejected alternative, and key trade-off

instrumentStandards.decisionQuestion: Does this individual security add a mandate-aligned benefit that a fund or ETF cannot provide without creating excessive idiosyncratic or concentration risk?
requiredAnalysis: Distinct portfolio purpose and evidence that a fund or ETF is not the better implementation
Business and return drivers, valuation context where relevant, and base/bear sensitivity
Liquidity, trading expenses, tax considerations, and client fit
Idiosyncratic risks and the evidence that makes them material
Position-size rationale, concentration limit, diversification effect, and monitoring or exit trigger
Concise alternative rejected and the key trade-off

issuerRealityCheck.title: Issuer Reality Check
issuerRealityCheck.decisionRule: Yield or recent return alone cannot support a recommendation. The committee must evidence the issuer's financial health, operating outlook, and relevance to the client's mandate.
issuerRealityCheck.applicability: Complete one concise snapshot for every direct individual security. For a selected fund or ETF, use look-through issuer analysis only when one holding or issuer is material to the exposure, concentration, or risk conclusion; do not create issuer work that duplicates the holding scorecard.
requiredFields: Security, issuer, exposure type, portfolio weight, source, and as-of date
Business model and principal revenue drivers
Industry and macro sensitivity under the committee's base and bear cases
Revenue, margin, and cash-flow trend using consistent periods
Interest coverage and debt-maturity considerations where relevant
One issuer-specific risk and the evidence that makes it material
Conclusion about client fit, allocation implication, and monitoring trigger

roleResponsibilities.responsibility: Own credit, duration, income, liquidity, and rate-risk evidence for fixed-income funds, ETFs, and any limited direct exposure.
Own equity-fund and ETF look-through review and the issuer analysis, idiosyncratic risk, and position-size rationale for any limited individual equity.
Explain how the committee's macro scenarios and the issuer's industry sensitivity affect the client-facing thesis and mandate fit.
Apply exposure, overlap, issuer-health, and concentration conclusions to final selection, weight, portfolio trade-offs, and monitoring or exit triggers.
Use material issuer and concentration evidence in portfolio-level stress tests and the residual-risk and hedge/no-hedge conclusion.

factSetWorkflow.title: FactSet Research and Evidence Record
factSetWorkflow.licenseBoundary: Use your licensed FactSet access to research and download data for your own course work. Submit the final project package and any required licensed-source supporting evidence privately through Canvas. Do not place FactSet captures, exports, credentials, completed proprietary data files, or student work in the public repository.
factSetWorkflow.navigationBoundary: FactSet layouts, entitlements, and labels can differ. Use course demonstrations and current FactSet support for navigation; this public guide defines the evidence standard, not a click path.

steps.action: Name the client guardrail, issuer claim, product comparison, or portfolio-risk input the FactSet research must test.
Research the relevant security, issuer, credit, financial-statement, fund/ETF, benchmark, holdings, or portfolio-risk data available in your licensed workspace.
Log what was retrieved, retrieval date, relevant metric or research item, entity/security, as-of period, and source or document reference as appropriate.
Explain what the evidence means for return drivers, risk, issuer health, product exposure, diversification, or client fit. Do not substitute copied output for analysis.
State how the evidence confirmed, qualified, contradicted, or changed the recommendation, then retain and submit the required licensed-source evidence privately through Canvas under course policy.

connections.application: Use current issuer, financial-statement, estimates, industry, ownership, or research evidence as appropriate to evaluate revenue and margin drivers, cash flow, liquidity, leverage, coverage, maturities, outlook, and issuer-specific risk.
Use relevant issue and issuer evidence for price/yield context, maturity and structure, duration or rate sensitivity, credit quality, spreads, liquidity, coverage, debt maturities, and downside risk.
Use relevant product, holdings, benchmark, style, performance, flow, risk, cost, liquidity, and overlap evidence while verifying official product facts in sponsor or filed documents when appropriate.
Use consistent financial periods and appropriate issuer evidence to interpret revenue, margins, cash flow, liquidity, leverage, and operating or industry sensitivity.
Use appropriately dated risk, return, exposure, correlation, or benchmark inputs and document their definitions, units, limitations, and role in the team calculation.

evidenceLogFields: Security, issuer, fund/ETF, benchmark, or portfolio input
Research question or decision claim tested
Source, screen, research, or document reference as appropriate
Data as-of period and retrieval date
Effect on the recommendation or portfolio input
Canvas submission item or evidence-file reference
Analyst owner, peer reviewer, and status

candidateTemplateColumns: Approved allocation sleeve and Phase 1 guardrail
Individual-security rationale, idiosyncratic risk, and position size if applicable
Final select/reject decision, concise alternative rejected, and key trade-off
securityQualityGate: The candidate set translates the approved allocation and client mandate into plausible implementations; the team does not research only its preferred product.
Each client portfolio targets 8–10 final holdings and never exceeds 10; eight is complete and no slot is filled without a distinct portfolio purpose.

Funds and ETFs are the primary vehicles. Individual securities are limited to two or three total, individual bonds are not required, and any individual security has added rationale, idiosyncratic-risk, and position-size evidence.
Every selection names the Phase 1 client guardrail it satisfies and the unresolved fact that could change it.
Every final holding has the consistent concise scorecard; alternatives rejected are compared concisely without full analysis of every screened name.
The team excludes candidates that duplicate exposure, create unnecessary concentration, lack appropriate liquidity, or fail the client mandate.
Return, yield, duration, credit, fee, trading-expense, benchmark, holdings, liquidity, overlap, and performance claims use appropriate approved sources and as-of dates.
Every direct individual security has an Issuer Reality Check; fund/ETF look-through is required only when an issuer is material to the exposure, concentration, or risk conclusion.

Each recommendation includes a FactSet retrieval record identifying the research retrieved, retrieval date, relevant metrics, source/document reference as appropriate, interpretation, and effect on the decision; licensed evidence is retained according to course policy.
The team distinguishes issuer risk, market risk, product risk, and client-suitability risk.
Each analyst records recommendations, alternatives rejected, and a key trade-off; a second member reviews the evidence trail.
The selected mix is evaluated for overlap and diversification as a portfolio, not only one instrument at a time.

portfolioWorkflow.action: Place analyst finalists into sleeves and assign tentative weights. Target 8–10 holdings, never exceed 10, and do not fill a slot without a distinct portfolio job.

The Portfolio Manager checks that weights total 100%, resources match the hypothetical AUM, and every holding traces to a Phase 1 guardrail and a verified selection decision; resolve overlap, concentration, and conflicting recommendations.
Calculate expected return and required course risk measures consistently; identify concentration, overlap, duration, credit, liquidity, and benchmark/style exposures.
Compare the integrated portfolio with every client objective, constraint, limit, and tripwire—not only the return target.

The Risk and Derivatives Analyst applies the approved Phase 1 bear assumptions without softening them, quantifies portfolio and dollar impacts, and identifies the residual risk and client goal most exposed.

Use the stress evidence to document either no hedge or one targeted derivative hedge. A hedge is valid only when it solves an identified residual risk; no hedge is fully valid when the evidence shows costs or trade-offs outweigh the benefit.
For every breach, record specific trades or constraint changes, explain the trade-off, recalculate the full portfolio, and confirm whether the revised portfolio passes.
Approve, revise, or reject each client portfolio. Record dissent, monitoring triggers, and action owners.

scenarioReveal.title: Scenario Reveal & required remediation
scenarioReveal.baseline: Submit the baseline allocation, IPS scorecard, and initial stress result at the instructor-designated checkpoint before the Scenario Reveal is released. Retain the submission confirmation; the baseline may not be rewritten after release.
scenarioReveal.release: The instructor releases a client-specific adverse-event packet after the baseline checkpoint. Record the packet ID, release date, named client goal or constraint tested, and exact inputs in the Scenario Reveal workbook tab.
scenarioReveal.test: Apply the released inputs exactly, quantify percentage and dollar impact, and state whether the affected client condition is a Pass, Warning, or Breach.
scenarioReveal.remediate: For every Breach, make a real security, sleeve, or weight change; explain the trade-off; then re-run the full scenario and IPS scorecard. If a released case unexpectedly passes, report it to the instructor rather than using the result to skip the checkpoint.
scenarioReveal.boundary: You may not change the client mandate, tripwire, or released scenario inputs to make the portfolio pass.

derivativeHedge.decisionRule: A derivative is optional, never performative. Use at most one targeted hedge per client portfolio and only when it addresses an identified residual risk that cannot be handled more appropriately through the holdings or weights.
derivativeHedge.noHedgeStandard: A no-hedge conclusion is complete when the Risk and Derivatives Analyst identifies the residual risk, explains why the portfolio should retain it, and supports why hedge cost, liquidity, complexity, basis risk, or other trade-offs outweigh the expected benefit.
proposalFields: Residual risk being hedged and stress evidence
Derivative instrument and why it targets that risk
Cost, liquidity, implementation demands, and trade-offs
Residual risk and basis or execution risk after the hedge

ipsComplianceChecks: Required return and priority client goals
Maximum volatility or other approved risk limit
Drawdown tripwire under the bear case
Liquidity reserve and known cash-flow dates
Legal, values-based, concentration, or other unique constraints
Diversification, benchmark/style, duration, and credit exposures
Total weights, hypothetical dollars, and implementability
stressTemplateColumns: IPS limit or client goal tested
adjustmentRecordFields: Old and revised weights and dollar amounts
Revised return, risk, liquidity, and bear-case results
Committee decision, dissent, owner, and monitoring trigger

roleIntegration.securityResponsibility: Audit every candidate against the approved client mandate and macro scenarios; reject any security whose rationale depends on an unapproved client fact.
roleIntegration.portfolioResponsibility: Confirm that the integrated allocation still serves the client's ranked goals and all RRTTLLU constraints.

roleIntegration.securityResponsibility: Own fixed-income funds and ETFs and any limited direct exposure, including income, yield, duration, credit quality, liquidity, costs, taxes, overlap, and rate-risk fit.
roleIntegration.portfolioResponsibility: Explain how the fixed-income sleeve changes income reliability, rate sensitivity, credit risk, liquidity, and bear-case protection.

roleIntegration.securityResponsibility: Own equity funds and ETFs and the limited use of individual equities, including benchmark/style mapping, holdings overlap, fees, trading, liquidity, taxes, idiosyncratic risk, and position size.
roleIntegration.portfolioResponsibility: Explain how the equity sleeve delivers the intended growth exposure and diversification without hidden duplication, unnecessary concentration, or avoidable cost.

roleIntegration.securityResponsibility: Integrate analyst finalists, resolve overlap and concentration, set the final 8–10 holdings and weights, and record recommendations rejected and explicit portfolio trade-offs.
roleIntegration.portfolioResponsibility: Own integration, weight and calculation checks, IPS scorecard coordination, implementation decisions, corrective trades, and the committee vote record.

roleIntegration.securityResponsibility: Challenge risk estimates and data comparability, identify residual portfolio risk, and own the evidence for one targeted hedge or a fully supported no-hedge conclusion.
roleIntegration.portfolioResponsibility: Own portfolio-level stress tests, breach escalation, residual-risk evidence, hedge sizing and trade-offs when proposed, and the full post-adjustment re-test.

portfolioQualityGate: Every final holding has a concise scorecard, a distinct portfolio job, an accountable role owner, a Phase 1 guardrail reference, and a concise alternative rejected.
The portfolio contains 8–10 final holdings and never more than 10; funds and ETFs are primary, individual securities total no more than two or three, and no unnecessary duplicate exposure remains.
Weights total 100% and dollar allocations reconcile to the hypothetical AUM.
Return and risk calculations use consistent as-of dates, units, and scenario assumptions.
The IPS scorecard tests all relevant objectives and constraints; the team does not declare compliance from one metric.
The bear case exactly carries forward the approved Phase 1 assumptions and shows both percentage and dollar impact.
Every warning or breach has a documented decision; every breach is corrected and re-tested before approval.

The Risk and Derivatives Analyst documents residual risk and either a supported no-hedge conclusion or one targeted hedge with instrument, size, cost, liquidity, trade-offs, remaining risk, and adjustment or removal condition.
The Portfolio Manager records final selection and weight decisions, overlap and concentration resolutions, alternatives rejected, and explicit portfolio trade-offs.
The final portfolio states monitoring triggers, remaining uncertainties, and what would cause the committee to reconvene.

phases.title: Frame the Mandate
phases.tagline: Agree on the world you are investing in and the rules you cannot break.
phases.keyQuestion: What must be true about markets and each client before we are willing to invest?
phases.objective: Establish one defensible 12-month market view and convert each assigned client profile into an approved investment mandate.
phases.gate: Approve or revise the common market view and all three client mandates. Portfolio construction cannot begin until the vote and action items are recorded.
phases.meetingMotion: Motion to approve the committee's market view and the investment mandate for each assigned client.

workstreams.title: Market view
workstreams.description: Read the historical data, compare the committee view with FactSet/FRED consensus, and build bull/base/bear scenarios.

workstreams.title: Client discovery
workstreams.description: Make a human-first judgment, complete the structured client role-play, and translate verified needs into RRTTLLU constraints.

workstreams.title: Decision log and guardrails
workstreams.description: Use a committee challenge to test the initial view, verify material claims, record final reasoning, and set criteria for later bonds, mutual funds/ETFs, allocation, and risk.

evidence: Human-first five-year macro read with source dates
FactSet/FRED consensus comparison and team forecast
Bull/base/bear scenarios with probabilities totaling 100%
RRTTLLU analysis for all three assigned clients
Return target, maximum volatility, and drawdown tripwire for each client
Analyst Decision Log showing initial judgment, committee challenge, verification, final reasoning, and downstream guardrail
Phase 1 decision record signed by all five members

phases.title: Build & Challenge
phases.tagline: Build the baseline, respond to the Scenario Reveal, and defend the revised portfolio.
phases.keyQuestion: Do 8–10 purposeful holdings—and no more than 10—implement the client mandate without avoidable overlap, concentration, cost, or residual risk?
phases.objective: Translate the approved allocation and client mandate into a focused portfolio, select funds and ETFs as the primary vehicles, limit individual securities, resolve portfolio trade-offs, and document stress-tested residual risk and a hedge or no-hedge conclusion.
phases.gate: Approve, revise, or reject each client portfolio. The baseline snapshot must precede the Scenario Reveal, and a revealed breach cannot receive approval without a documented corrective trade and re-test.
phases.meetingMotion: Motion to approve the proposed portfolio and risk-mitigation plan for each assigned client.

workstreams.title: A · Capital-market expectations
workstreams.description: Convert the market view into expected returns, volatility, correlations, and Solver constraints for base and bear cases.

workstreams.title: B · Securities & implementation
workstreams.description: Translate the approved allocation into candidates, use concise scorecards to select 8–10 holdings, reject alternatives briefly, and keep funds and ETFs as the primary vehicles.

workstreams.title: C · Scenario Reveal & corrective action
workstreams.description: Integrate final weights, resolve overlap and concentration, submit the baseline, apply the instructor-issued adverse-event packet, test residual risk, and document corrective trades plus a hedge or no-hedge conclusion.

evidence: Base and bear CME inputs with cited rationale
Solver output and constraint checks for each client
Focused candidate set translated from the approved allocation and client mandate
Final portfolio of 8–10 holdings, never more than 10, using funds and ETFs as the primary vehicles and no more than two or three individual securities
Concise final-holding scorecards covering exposure/role, cost and trading expenses, liquidity, holdings/sector/style overlap, diversification contribution, key risks, and client-mandate fit
Added rationale, idiosyncratic-risk, and position-size evidence for every individual security; individual bonds are not required
Concise comparisons and rejection reasons for realistic alternatives without full analysis of every screened name
Issuer Reality Check for every direct individual security and only material look-through issuer exposures within selected funds or ETFs
FactSet Research and Evidence Log for every recommended security and material portfolio-risk input

Integrated allocation with a purpose, owner, Phase 1 guardrail, risk contribution, and monitoring trigger for every holding, plus the Portfolio Manager's overlap, concentration, final-weight, and trade-off decisions
Portfolio-level stress tests and the Risk and Derivatives Analyst's residual-risk evidence
Supported no-hedge conclusion or one targeted derivative hedge with risk, instrument, size, cost, liquidity, trade-offs, residual risk, and adjustment/removal condition
Locked baseline snapshot and instructor-issued Scenario Reveal log for every client
Full IPS compliance scorecard and Scenario Reveal result against each approved tripwire and relevant constraint
Before/after record, trade-off, and full re-test for every corrective trade
AI audit entries linked to human verification
Phase 2 decision record signed by all five members

Baseline snapshot plus completed Scenario Reveal, remediation, IPS compliance, and re-test record
Phase 2 decision record with client-by-client votes

phases.title: Defend the Recommendation
phases.tagline: Make the recommendation visible, auditable, and defensible under pressure.
phases.keyQuestion: Can every committee member defend the same evidence-linked recommendation to the panel?
phases.objective: Integrate the committee's work into a concise decision package and defend the client recommendations before an investment-committee panel.
phases.gate: Issue the final recommendation, record dissent or reservations, and defend the evidence. Every member must answer questions outside the workstream they led.
phases.meetingMotion: Motion to issue the committee's final recommendation and implementation plan for all assigned clients.

canvasSubmissions.title: Canvas Submission Workflow
canvasSubmissions.purpose: Use one clearly named team submission at each approval gate so the committee's decision trail, owned work, and licensed evidence remain private and reviewable.
canvasSubmissions.authority: The Canvas assignment controls the due date, points, availability window, and attempt policy. This guide controls the required package, filenames, and public/private boundary.
sharedRules: One designated submitter uploads the complete package for the Canvas group; all five members confirm the receipt before the deadline.
Use Team01, Team02, and so on in filenames. Replace the two-digit placeholder; do not add student names to filenames.
Keep formulas live in required XLSX files. Export narrative and exhibit deliverables to PDF unless PPTX or XLSX is explicitly required.
Put only licensed FactSet evidence in the private evidence ZIP. Do not place credentials, raw student data, or unrelated downloads in the bundle.
Before submitting, open every file, confirm the three assigned clients and five analyst owners are visible, and verify that all cited as-of dates match the analysis.
After upload, open the Canvas submission receipt and confirm that every required filename appears. A local file or public-repository link is not a submission.

assessment.presentationRubricName: BUS331 Investment Project Presentation and Defense

writtenCriteria.standard: Claims, calculations, formulas, sources, FactSet retrieval records, as-of dates, and portfolio metrics are correct, comparable, traceable, and interpreted; required licensed evidence is submitted privately through Canvas and AI output is never treated as evidence.

Each client portfolio contains 8–10 holdings and never more than 10; funds and ETFs are primary, individual securities total no more than two or three, final holdings have concise scorecards, and realistic alternatives are rejected briefly without duplicate exposure or unnecessary concentration.
Each recommendation traces to Phase 1 client needs and guardrails, and the IPS scorecard tests all relevant objectives and RRTTLLU constraints.

Final selection and weights, diversification, overlap, concentration, portfolio trade-offs, stress results, breaches, corrective trades, re-tests, and the supported hedge or no-hedge conclusion form one internally consistent portfolio decision.

For each student, role-specific evidence is identifiable and peer-reviewed, and the Analyst Decision Log records recommendation(s), alternative(s) rejected, a key trade-off, contribution to integration or residual-risk decisions, and the link to the committee vote.

oralCriteria.standard: Within the presentation's compact investment-committee defense, each member answers targeted questions for their role, uses relevant evidence and calculations, acknowledges uncertainty, and defends or revises the judgment under challenge.
Each member demonstrates command of owned evidence and can explain their recommendation, alternative rejected, key trade-off, Decision Log contribution, verification, and limitations.

The committee presents one coherent chain from client discovery through the focused 8–10 holding selection, final weights, overlap/concentration decisions, stress results, hedge or no-hedge conclusion, correction, and final recommendation.
Members can show where client needs changed the portfolio, explain the strongest bear case and residual risk, and defend compliance, corrective action, and the hedge or no-hedge conclusion.
The team communicates concisely as client-focused professionals and uses legible exhibits that make the recommendation, trade-offs, and evidence visible.

questions: Which Phase 1 client fact or guardrail most changed the final portfolio, and where can the committee see that change?
Which macro assumption matters most to this recommendation, and what evidence would cause the team to revise it?
Which unresolved client information gap remains material, and how did the portfolio avoid pretending it was known?
Why does the selected fixed-income exposure fit the client's cash-flow horizon better than the strongest alternative?
What happens to price and income if rates or credit spreads move against the position, and which duration or credit evidence supports that answer?
What did the Issuer Reality Check reveal about cash flow, leverage, interest coverage, maturities, and the largest issuer-specific risk?
Why does the selected equity fund or ETF deliver the needed exposure better than the strongest alternative after costs, liquidity, overlap, and style or sector concentration?
If the portfolio includes an individual equity, why is it superior to a fund or ETF for that role, what is its idiosyncratic risk, and why is the position size appropriate?
Which equity candidate did you reject, and what key trade-off separated it from your recommendation?
Which analyst recommendations did you integrate, resize, or reject, and what explicit portfolio trade-off drove each decision?
Where did you resolve overlap or concentration, and why are the final 8–10 holdings and weights better than the strongest alternative mix?
If the committee rejects one proposed adjustment, what alternative preserves the client goal and what new trade-off does it create?
Which residual risk contributes most to the bear-case loss, and which client goal is therefore most exposed?
Why is the supported conclusion hedge or no hedge, and what evidence makes that conclusion preferable to changing the underlying holdings or weights?
If a hedge is proposed, explain the instrument, size, cost, liquidity, trade-offs, residual risk, and adjustment or removal condition.
What was the team's strongest initial judgment that changed after AI challenge and human verification?
Which FactSet retrieval most affected the recommendation, how did you interpret it, and where is the licensed-source evidence retained under course policy?
Which source or calculation carries the most decision weight, and what are its limitations?
What is the strongest reasonable case against the final recommendation?
What monitoring trigger would force the committee to reconvene before the normal review date?
